correctness.rationale: At predator-free y>0,z=0, infected-prey stationarity yields x=nu(alpha+y)/beta. Substituting into susceptible-prey equation yields exact quadratic F(y)=r(alpha+y)[beta K-alpha nu-(beta+nu)y]-beta^2 K y. If beta K<=alpha nu, F<0 for y>0. If A=beta K-alpha nu>0, leading coefficient negative, F(0)>0, hence one positive root (the positive and negative roots of the sign-changed quadratic have opposite signs). This proves threshold iff beta K/(alpha nu)>1 and uniqueness. Independent exact substitutions verify printed-proposition counterexample (r,alpha,nu,beta,K)=(1,1,1,2,2/5), F=-(15y^2+24y+1)/5, and feasible K=1 giving F=1-6y-3y^2. No predator-interior/delay bifurcation conclusion claimed.

Naji–Hasan has mass-action/recovery; Mortoja–Panja–Mondal is related but not shown to imply this saturated-incidence correction.
